Title: Nationwide randomised trial evaluating elective neck dissection for early stage oral cancer (SEND study) with meta-analysis and concurrent real-world cohort
Author: Hutchison et al.
Comment: M_diff here is the reported 5-year absolute risk difference in percentage points (END minus resection only), not a mean difference. The paper also reports an "all time points" ITT DFS HR of 0.71 (95% CI 0.48-1.04, p=0.08) and a footnote variant excluding 3 non-oral-cavity patients (HR 0.64 up to 5 years, 0.69 all time points, no CIs given). Per-arm DFS event counts were in Supplementary Table 2 (not available in this text); only the total of 109 events is reported. Trial stopped recruitment early (250 of planned 620).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Neck dissection (elective END) and resection') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomised controlled trial (multicentre, 1:1, central allocation concealment)
domain: head and neck oncology / oral squamous cell carcinoma surgery
Participant type: Adults (>=16 years) with histopathologically confirmed T1/T2 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma
Recruitment source: 27 hospitals in the UK National Cancer Research Network (25 hospitals for the randomised cohort)
Outcome measurement: Hazard ratio (Cox proportional hazards), END with resection versus resection only
effect_direction: favours elective neck dissection (HR 0.66 < 1, longer DFS with END)

Title: Prospective randomized study of selective neck dissection versus observation for N0 neck of early tongue carcinoma
Author: Yuen AP-W, Ho CM, Chow TL, Tang LC, Cheung WY, Ng RW-M, Wei WI, et al.
Comment: No hazard ratio, no observed/expected event counts, and no variance statistics are reported; only 5-year KM percentages and the log-rank p value (p = .89). An HR cannot be derived from the reported percentages alone; per-arm event counts plus this log-rank p (see the companion row) would be needed for a Parmar/Peto indirect estimate. The paper defines DFS as time from first operation to death or last follow-up, i.e. a disease-specific mortality endpoint rather than strictly time-to-recurrence.; unsupported or insufficient statistic type
domain: head and neck oncology / surgical management of the clinically node-negative neck
Participant type: Adults with AJCC stage I-II squamous cell carcinoma of the oral tongue and ultrasonographically N0 neck
Recruitment source: Multicenter: Queen Mary, Kwong Wah and United Christian Hospitals (with referrals from Queen Elizabeth, Ruttonjee and Yan Chai Hospitals), Hong Kong, 1996-2004
Outcome measurement: Actuarial 5-year disease-specific survival percentage per arm, Kaplan-Meier curves compared by log-rank test
effect_direction: essentially no difference, trivially favours elective (89% vs 87%, p = 0.89)

Title: bbd556e6_NEJMoa1506007 — Elective versus Therapeutic Neck Dissection in Node-Negative Oral Cancer
Author: D'Cruz et al.
Comment: P value reported only as "P<0.001" (log-rank); recorded as 0.001 threshold. Interim analysis of the first 500 of 596 randomized patients after early stopping for benefit; percentages entered in group_*_mean_perc are 3-year Kaplan–Meier DFS rates, not simple proportions. Adjusted HR (0.44; 95% CI 0.33–0.57) also reported but the unadjusted ITT HR was selected per the plan. SE(log HR) not computed here; derivable from the reported 95% CI.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Elective-surgery group (ipsilateral neck dissection at time of primary surgery)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults aged 18–75 years with previously untreated, lateralized T1/T2 clinically node-negative oral squamous-cell carcinoma (tongue, floor of mouth, or buccal mucosa)
Recruitment source: Single centre: Tata Memorial Centre, Mumbai, India (screened 1281, randomized 596; first 500 analysed)
Outcome measurement: Unadjusted hazard ratio for disease-free survival (elective vs. therapeutic neck dissection) with 95% CI; 3-year DFS rates; number of recurrences per arm
effect_direction: favours elective neck dissection (HR 0.45 < 1, longer DFS with elective surgery)

Title: Supraomohyoid Neck Dissection in the Treatment of T1/T2 Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Oral Cavity
Author: Kligerman J, Lima RA, Soares JR, Prado L, Dias FL, Freitas EQ, Olivatto LO
Comment: No hazard ratio, 95% CI, variance, or overall log-rank statistic (O-E/V) is reported for the whole-arm disease-free survival comparison; only Kaplan-Meier percentages at 3.5 years. The only P = 0.05 reported in this section refers to a subgroup (tumour thickness >4 mm) benefit on DFS, not the overall arm comparison. A DFS hazard ratio therefore cannot be computed directly from this row without the per-arm event counts (see the recurrence/event-count row).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection (RSOND)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: Adults with previously untreated T1/T2 N0 squamous cell carcinoma of the oral tongue or floor of mouth (median age 57, range 34-95; 52 men, 15 women)
Recruitment source: Head and Neck Service, Cancer Hospital, National Cancer Institute, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 1987-1992
Outcome measurement: Percent disease-free at 3.5 years (Kaplan-Meier actuarial method)
effect_direction: favours elective supraomohyoid neck dissection (72% vs 49% disease-free at 3.5 years)

Title: Prophylactic Neck Dissection in Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Oral Tongue: A Prospective Randomized Study
Author: Fakih, Rao & Patel
Comment: No hazard ratio, no 95% CI, no log-rank statistic, no observed/expected events and no p-value are reported anywhere in the paper — only the statement "statistically not significant". Therefore neither a direct HR nor a Peto/Parmar indirect HR estimate can be derived; only raw disease-free proportions are available. Arm labelling: the RESULTS sentence states "64% in group A and 47% in group B", which contradicts the Abstract ("higher (64% vs. 47%) in the group receiving prophylactic neck dissection"), Discussion point 3 ("better in the hemiglossectomy + RND group ... (64% vs. 47%)") and Figure 1 (hemiglossectomy only, n=21: 10/21 = 47%); arms were therefore assigned as prophylactic/elective = 64% and therapeutic = 47%. group_1_events left empty: 64% of 14 implies 9/14 but no such fraction is stated verbatim in the text. Interim report of an ongoing trial (35 of planned 100 patients).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group B: hemiglossectomy + simultaneous prophylactic (elective) ipsilateral radical neck dissection') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (prospective, two-arm, interim analysis)
domain: head and neck oncology / surgical oncology
Participant type: adults with histologically proven T1-T2 N0M0 squamous cell carcinoma of the oral tongue
Recruitment source: Department of Surgery, Tata Memorial Hospital, Bombay, India
Outcome type: dichotomous (time-to-event reported only as proportion disease-free)
Outcome measurement: Percentage of patients disease-free at last follow-up (Figures 1 and 2 evolution-of-disease trees)
Outcome variable: Overall disease-free survival (proportion alive and disease-free)
effect_direction: favours prophylactic/elective neck dissection (64% vs 47% disease-free; stated as not statistically significant)
